title: Insight list default ordering must use an indexed column
answers: Insights API list without order param is very slow
Paginating /api/projects/:id/insights/ takes tens of seconds per page
order_queryset falls back to sorting on unindexed column
body:
Symptom: Listing insights via the API with no `order` param takes tens of seconds per page and pins a web worker; every offset page repeats the cost.
Root cause: products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/insight.py:order_queryset defaulted to `order_by("order")`. `Insight.order` is a vestigial nullable, unindexed column, so Postgres scanned and sorted the whole project.
Fix pattern: default to an ordering covered by an existing index: `order_by("-last_modified_at", "-pk")`, backed by partial index `dashboarditem_team_lmod_idx` on (team_id, -last_modified_at) WHERE NOT deleted. `-pk` is a tiebreaker for stable pagination.
Constraints: don't add an index on `order` (NULL for nearly all rows). Keep the `with_last_viewed_at` annotation, since both list serializers return `last_viewed_at`. The `search` branch still returns the queryset unordered (relevance ranking). Changing the default changes response order for clients that send no `order`. The PR did not run a production EXPLAIN.
applies: Insight list endpoint default sort in products/product_analytics/backend/presentation/insight.py
